a8c95ec14e.q: What is ATAS VC's investment thesis and what industries does the firm focus on?
a8c95ec14e.a: ATAS VC is a pre-seed focused venture firm investing in American necessities real technologies to solve real problems for real people. The firm backs pre-seed companies working across energy, manufacturing, agriculture and other core American industries, focusing on hard tech—applied robotics, complex AI, and technology with engineering risk rather than existential science risk where the core science is already validated.

f97dfe66b1.q: Why did Andrew Chan leave Builders VC to start his own venture capital firm?
f97dfe66b1.a: Chan left Builders VC because they were moving toward growth equity and Series A investing, which he wasn't enjoying. He took time off for personal reasons and realized there was a fundamental lack of good science in venture capital, especially on the deep tech side, with insufficient scientific underwriting standards. He found himself in a stable cash position and able to take risk, so he started ATAS VC to build a firm with higher scientific standards and less focus on hype wave fundraising.

77fba1bcae.q: What is the difference between hard tech and deep tech venture investing according to Andrew Chan?
77fba1bcae.a: Chan distinguishes hard tech from deep tech by focusing on engineering risk rather than science risk. He avoids investing in quantum or fusion where existential questions remain about feasibility. Hard tech investments require validated science but may have scalability challenges—the question is whether throwing more engineering talent at the problem will eventually solve it, not whether the core science fundamentally works.
